solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: In court, Connolly will appear in minute and second

parts.note: minute (pronounced my-NEWT) means tiny, little
a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: A courtroom appearance by someone called Connolly, scheduled in fractions of time.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'court' is a tennis court, not a law court: Maureen Connolly, the 1950s American tennis champion, was nicknamed this.
explanation.definitionFit: Nickname of tennis player Maureen Connolly, winner of the Grand Slam in 1953.

clue.text: Time to split releases

definitions.meaning: a call to leave, split being slang for depart

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a cry of departure and a verb phrase for freeing one's grip.

clue.text: History file is being broadcast about you

definitions.text: History file is being broadcast about you

indicators.note: the anagram letters go round the letter for 'you'
broadcast means scattered, so these letters are spread out and rearranged

parts.note: U is text-speak for you

explanation.surface: A television documentary of someone's past is going out on air, all about them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being broadcast' scrambles HISTORYFILEIS, which goes 'about' U. The whole clue also describes the old TV show, in which a guest's life story was presented to them on air.
explanation.definitionFit: The long-running British TV programme surprised a celebrity with a review of their life, a broadcast history about the guest.

clue.text: Very much like pupil at Harrow?

indicators.note: a harrow breaks up soil, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking whether something resembles a boy at Harrow, the English public school.
explanation.walkthrough: Harrow is a famous English boarding school, but here 'Harrow' is a verb, breaking up PUPILAT.
explanation.definitionFit: To relish something greatly, like a cat eagerly drinking cream, is the idiom.

clue.text: Circus performers overhead, with big 6

parts.note: the comedy team of the Flying Circus (overhead = flying), who also produced the Big Red Book

explanation.surface: Trapeze artists above the ring, along with something large.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 is RED BOOK: the comedy troupe's TV show was the Flying Circus, and their 1971 book was the Big Red Book.
explanation.definitionFit: The British comedy group made the Flying Circus series and published the Big Red Book.

clue.text: Vehicle having run out in a religious spot

indicators.note: the cricket letters are placed inside the word for a religious mark

parts.note: a tika is a Hindu mark worn on the forehead
RO is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out

explanation.surface: A car stranded after running dry at a place of worship.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman can be 'run out' (RO on the scorecard). A tika is the coloured mark Hindus wear on the forehead.
explanation.definitionFit: A Russian carriage drawn by three horses abreast is a horse-drawn vehicle.

clue.text: Spooner has to sleep with black bird in 2&15's main feature

indicators.note: Spooner signals swapping the opening sounds of two words

parts.note: bed as a verb, to go to sleep or put to bed
a rook is a black crow-like bird

explanation.surface: A reverend must bed down beside a dark bird.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of BED ROOK gives the big book that presenters carried to surprise the guest on the TV show at 2 and 15.
explanation.definitionFit: The show's presenter carried a large crimson volume holding the guest's life story, its trademark prop.

clue.text: Isn't suffering? (Sauce that's hot, not half fuelling fire!)

indicators.note: the sauce goes into the scrambled letters, as fuel goes into a fire
suffering suggests something in a bad way, so these letters are disturbed
only one half of the sauce's doubled name is kept

parts.note: piri-piri is a fiery chilli sauce

explanation.surface: A question about pain, then an aside about a hot sauce stoking flames.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering' turns ISNT into INST, and 'fuelling' puts PIRI, which is half of PIRIPIRI ('not half'), inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To fire someone up is to animate or encourage them, the sense of this verb.

clue.text: Useful item for building, outside which surprise bearer of 6 is a plant

indicators.note: the presenter's name goes outside the builder's tool

parts.note: Michael Aspel presented the life-story show, bringing the big red book to surprised guests
a hod is a trough used to carry bricks on a building site

explanation.surface: A builder's tool wrapped by someone delivering a surprise turns out to be a spy.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Aspel was a later presenter of the TV show at 2 and 15; a hod is the bricklayer's carrying trough. 'plant' looks like a spy.
explanation.definitionFit: This lily family flower is a plant, linked in Greek myth to the fields of the dead.

clue.text: On LSD in the execution of the Light Fantastic

definitions.meaning: having a hallucinogenic experience on acid

definitions.text: in the execution of the Light Fantastic
definitions.meaning: to trip the light fantastic is to dance

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is being high on acid; the other comes from the idiom for dancing, to trip the light fantastic.

clue.text: A D-day drink makes sense

parts.note: the letter D as printed, then D for day
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Having a drink on the day of the invasion seems logical.
explanation.definitionFit: When a story is coherent it is said to tally or be consistent, the idiom here.

clue.text: Frightful time to cut, and hard to swallow

indicators.note: the time letter cuts into the word for frightful

parts.note: grisly means gruesome, frightful

explanation.surface: A horrible moment for surgery, and a hard pill to swallow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hard to swallow' looks like 'unbelievable' but is literal: tough, chewy meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat full of tough cartilage is difficult to chew and get down.

clue.text: Banger making singers, touring at last, cross

indicators.note: touring means moving around, and at last puts a letter at the end of the word for singers

parts.note: a choir is a group of singers
a zo (or dzo) is a cross between a yak and a cow

explanation.surface: Something explosive turns a touring group of singers angry.
explanation.walkthrough: In CHOIR the I travels to the end ('touring at last') to give CHORI. Banger is British slang for a sausage.
explanation.definitionFit: This spicy Spanish pork sausage is a banger, British slang for any sausage.

clue.text: Dish of macaroni and ham from author of little 6

indicators.note: to dish is to ruin or wreck, so these letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A plate of pasta with ham, served up by a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dish' looks like a plate of food but is the verb to ruin. 6 is RED BOOK, so 'little 6' is the Little Red Book.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chinese Communist leader's quotations were compiled as the Little Red Book.

clue.text: Now do debtors dread it? Maybe, and pack in a panic!

indicators.note: panic suggests frantic disorder, so these letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: Wondering whether people in debt fear the moment of reckoning, and urging them to flee.
explanation.definitionFit: The moment of revenge or repayment is the hour that those who owe money fear.

clue.text: Weird new action replay Nero's not seen

indicators.note: new signals that these letters are made over in a fresh order
the emperor's letters are removed from the pool and so are not seen

parts.note: the emperor's name, the possessive adding no letter

explanation.surface: A strange new replay of footage that the emperor missed.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of ACTION REPLAY, remove NERO's letters ('not seen'), and rearrange the rest ('new').
explanation.definitionFit: Something unusual or out of the norm is weird, a close synonym.

clue.text: See 2
The Enemy Within: John, a vagrant, enters resort for bombing

indicators.note: the jumbled name goes inside the jumbled resort
a bombed place is wrecked, so these letters are blown apart and rearranged
a vagrant wanders, so these letters wander out of order

explanation.surface: A wandering man infiltrates a holiday resort to plant a bomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vagrant' jumbles JOHNA into JANHO, which 'enters' TRORSE, the jumble of RESORT signalled by 'for bombing'.
explanation.definitionFit: The wooden horse that smuggled Greek soldiers into Troy is the classic infiltrator, and the term for disguised malware.

clue.text: A foursome getting together in order to secure a new Asian currency

indicators.note: the four letters hold the next two inside them

parts.note: four consecutive letters of the alphabet standing together

explanation.surface: Four people combining in sequence to obtain a fresh foreign currency.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'foursome' is a run of four alphabet letters in order, F G H I.
explanation.definitionFit: The monetary unit of Afghanistan, a country in Central Asia.

clue.text: Play-mate's finished it

definitions.meaning: checkmate concludes the final phase of a chess game

explanation.definitionFit: It is the title of a Beckett drama and also the final stage of a chess game, ended by checkmate.

clue.text: Sustained melody with time roused love

indicators.note: roused means stirred up, and in a down clue up means the letters read backwards

parts.note: a tune is a melody
O is love, a nil score in tennis

explanation.surface: A tune that lasts, with timing that stirred feelings of love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roused' (raised up) turns TUNET into TENUT in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This musical direction tells the player to hold a note for its full value.

clue.text: Lover of opera 'an ex-peddler of drugs', as she confirms

parts.note: she would say I of herself
someone who once peddled has sold
E is ecstasy, a drug

explanation.surface: An opera heroine admits to a past dealing narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the quoted phrase as her own admission: I SOLD E, E being ecstasy.
explanation.definitionFit: Wagner's heroine is the beloved of Tristan in his opera Tristan und Isolde.

clue.text: Secretary — poorly-clad example to us all

parts.note: PA is a personal assistant, a secretary
wearing nothing but a rag: rag on

explanation.surface: A shabbily dressed secretary is nonetheless a model employee.
explanation.definitionFit: A model of excellence, a perfect example for everyone to follow.

clue.text: Surprise bearer of 6, one with information about medic

parts.note: A is one, the indefinite article

indicators.note: the news word goes around the doctor's abbreviation

parts.note: news is information
DR is the abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: Someone bringing a shock, along with word concerning a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 is RED BOOK: Eamonn Andrews was the original presenter who surprised guests with it.
explanation.definitionFit: Eamonn Andrews hosted the life-story TV show, springing the red book on unsuspecting guests.

clue.text: Caroline's first capital kiss, and its possible end-point?

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the name is taken

parts.note: Lima is the capital of Peru
X is a kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: Caroline's first kiss in a capital city, and where it might lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'its' refers back to the kiss: where kissing might end up.
explanation.definitionFit: The peak or culmination, here a suggestive one, is the high point of an encounter.

clue.text: Cambridge college's redesigned meal menu

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: something redesigned has its parts rearranged into a new pattern

explanation.surface: A university college has reworked its dining menu.
explanation.definitionFit: This college of Cambridge University was founded in 1584 by Sir Walter Mildmay.

clue.text: Chemist's whopper, putting cart before horse?

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: the back half of the phrase is moved to the front

parts.note: a whopper is a big lie

explanation.surface: A pharmacist's tall tale, getting things in the wrong order.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the two halves of BIG LIE; 'Chemist' is not a pharmacy but a scientist.
explanation.definitionFit: Justus von Liebig was the 19th-century German organic chemist behind meat extract and fertiliser research.

clue.text: My Jo? No longer, by the look of it!

definitions.text: My Jo? No longer, by the look of it!

parts.words: My Jo? No longer, by the look of it!
parts.note: jo is Scots for sweetheart; read in the past tense, a darling who was loved and is no longer

explanation.surface: Someone wondering whether their sweetheart is still theirs.
explanation.walkthrough: Jo is Scots for a sweetheart, as in Burns's 'John Anderson, my jo'. The phrase looks like 'someone who was loved' but means a dear one.
explanation.definitionFit: A dear person, a close relative or partner, is a cherished person, a euphemism often used of the dead.
